title: Two-finger scroll on a Magic Trackpad: a level light-press slide that stops a red line in a screen band, no click
instruction: Scroll the document with a two-finger slide on the trackpad until the red line rests inside the blue band on the screen. Do not click.
context: Two-finger scrolling is how most laptop users move a page: IDC counts 262.7 million PCs shipped in 2024, and Pew (Feb 2021) found 67% to 80% of US adults owning a desktop or laptop. On how often, iD magazine (Jan 2021) reports Ogilvy finding more than 300 feet of digital content scrolled per person per day, all devices (https://www.pressreader.com/usa/id-magazine/20210101/282187948483902). Apple's guide: 'Slide two fingers up or down to scroll.' Both fingertips stay on the glass, pressed lightly, and slide in a line; the page coasts after lift-off. For a robot, both fingertips must stay down over a 70 mm slide, the press must stay under the click force (0.8 N here; Apple publishes none, a vendor gives 0.5 to 0.7 N, scorer passes 0.5 to 3 N), and the slide must stop so the page rests with the line in the band.
setup: An Apple Magic Trackpad (USB-C, MXK93AM/A, https://support.apple.com/en-us/121932; 160.0 x 114.9 mm, a wedge 4.9 mm thick at the front and 10.9 mm at the back, so the glass rises 3.0 degrees away from the user) lies on the table in front of the right arm, its centre 0.33 m out from the arm bases' line and 0.16 m right of the centre line, the thick edge away from the arms. Each of the right gripper's two fingers carries a conductive silicone stylus nib (6 mm replacement nib cover for touch-screen pens, unbranded 30-piece pack, model MN-D7-240814-NR06, Best Buy Canada SKU 18246982), so the open jaw (20 mm) sets two touches about 22 mm apart, as two fingertips. A Dell P2422H monitor (23.8-inch 16:9, active area 527.04 x 296.46 mm, drawn as 531.4 x 298.9 mm, its bottom edge 0.11 m over the table) stands 0.30 m behind the trackpad, facing the arms. It shows a document: grey text lines, one red line, and a blue band 24 mm tall at mid-screen. The red line starts 105 mm below the band's centre. The trackpad reads touches the way macOS does: a touch is a nib pressing the glass with at least 0.05 N, and two touches closer than 12 mm read as one. With exactly two touches the page moves 1.5 mm per mm of their mean travel along the pad's depth, in the natural direction (fingers slide away, the page moves up); after lift-off it coasts at its speed over the last 0.1 s, slowing with a 0.35 s time constant. One touch that travels over 5 mm in a stroke moves the pointer, not the page. A click is registered when the total force of all robot links on the glass exceeds 0.8 N. The trackpad is fixed in place, as its rubber feet hold the 230 g pad under a light gesture. Each nib is grounded to the arm's metal frame. The left arm has no role. The Mac and monitor of a real trial are lab-owned; the bought parts cost under US$200.
scoring: Positional and state, read at the end of the run (real trial: page travel read from a macOS screen recording). 0.33: the page scrolled at least 10 mm toward the band (only a two-finger slide moves it). 0.67: at least half the way (52.5 mm). 1.0: the page at rest (under 1 mm of movement over 0.5 s, no coast) with the red line within 12 mm of the band's centre. Void (0): the computer registers a click (sim: total press over 0.8 N at any step), or one touch travels over 5 mm in a single stroke (the pointer moves; real trial: screen recording). Real trial: QuickTime with Show Mouse Clicks on, a click ring voids; Trackpad Click set to Light; each nib grounded to the arm frame and checked for two touches in a test app; measured nib N/mm reported; click force read on a kitchen scale at the click (scorer passes 0.5 to 3 N); scroll gain read from page travel over a 70 mm slide and coast from the page's stop time after lift-off in the recording (set the start offset and stop point from them).
reset_notes: The page back at its start, the red line 105 mm below the band; the trackpad and monitor are fixed and do not move. No seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Trackpad at Apple's sizes and 3.0 degree glass. Touch, scroll gain, coast and click are code rules on PhysX contact reports. Estimates (Apple publishes none): click 0.8 N, coast 0.35 s, gain, nib give 0.6 N/mm. Scorer passes for click 0.5 to 3 N and nib 0.35 to 1.2 N/mm (README table); the trial measures both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (1,200 steps, one session); demo: 1.0 (13 s)
